seasonal

/SEE-zun-ul/ — rhymes with reasonable · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Seasonal means occurring only at a particular time of year, tied to the seasons.

The little shop only sells seasonal produce, switching its shelves from strawberries to pumpkins as the year turns.

Example

The store's seasonal decorations transformed from snowflakes and silver in December to shamrocks and green in March.

Seasonal makes clear that these decorations are specifically tied to the seasons, changing as spring arrives. 'Temporary' or 'changing' wouldn't capture the exact sense of being connected to the natural seasons themselves.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

cyclical: Cyclical means moving through a repeating cycle of phases — boom and bust, wake and sleep — of any length, from minutes to decades. Seasonal is cyclical in one specific way: tied to the natural seasons of the year. The moon's phases are cyclical; a beach town's crowds are seasonal.

annual: Annual means happening once each year — an annual checkup, an annual report — landing on roughly the same date. Seasonal ties a thing to a stretch of the year rather than to one yearly occurrence: strawberries are seasonal all June, not annual on June 1st. Annual counts occurrences; seasonal names the time of year.

recurrent: Recurrent means happening again and again — recurrent dreams, recurrent injuries — with no schedule implied. Seasonal pins the return to a specific part of the year: the thing comes back because the calendar does. A recurrent cough strikes at random; a seasonal one arrives every spring with the pollen.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

year-round: available or happening in every season

perennial: enduring year after year without pause

Where it sits · how tightly tied to the yearly calendar — permanent → temporary → periodic → seasonal

permanent vs. seasonal: Permanent describes what never changes at all — a granite statue in the plaza is permanent — so it cannot capture the yearly coming-and-going that seasonal names.

temporary vs. seasonal: A detour during road construction is temporary — it simply won't last — but temporary says nothing about returning on nature's calendar the way seasonal does.

periodic vs. seasonal: A bus that arrives every twenty minutes is periodic, recurring on a schedule, but only something tied to the year's natural quarters — like geese flying south each autumn — earns the word seasonal.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — season

Root — season: the sowing time (Latin satio, 'a sowing,' which drifted through Old French seson into English; the ancient 'sow' root also grows seed and disseminate, 'to scatter like seed')

Suffix — -al

Suffix — -al: relating to, of the kind of

Put it together

Put it together: Season (the sowing time — Latin satio, 'a sowing,' which drifted through Old French seson into English) + -al (relating to) tells this word's true story: satio first meant planting season, then stretched to name every recurring stretch of the year — so seasonal means relating to those recurring times. The same ancient 'sow' root family gives English seed and disseminate — 'to scatter like seed.'

Use the root in a new word: disseminate

Use the root in a new word: disseminate: Volunteers helped disseminate the flyers across the whole neighborhood, scattering them door to door like seeds.

Strength Check

Word Choice

neutral / everyday

Use seasonal for anything tied to the natural seasons—foods that grow at certain times, weather patterns tied to specific months, or products only sold during certain times of year. For something that simply lasts a limited time unrelated to seasons, use temporary instead.
